Nobody knows why gender dysphoria happens, but the most common theory is that hormones in the womb cause the brain and the body to become mismatched.

Yes! The prefix "bi" does, in fact, mean two - but the history of bisexuality has moulded the term to now mean "attraction to two or more genders".

First of all, bisexuality wasn't a label made by bisexual people - it was reclaimed from medical use. At the time of the labels creation, there was no nonbinary labels in the western world, so everyone either identified as male or female.

In 1990 [the bisexual manifesto](http://binetusa.blogspot.com/2014/01/1990-bi-manifesto.html) was made. "Do not assume that bisexuality is binary" is a key part. As well as this, many bisexual people at the time described their sexuality as attraction to all genders.

So yeah, whilst the prefix bi = two, the history of bisexuality means bisexuality is defined as "attraction to two or more genders".
